title: Finite basic-open covers generate one under ideal H1 vanishing
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. Let $s\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be finite and suppose that the opens $X_f$ for $f\in s$ cover $X$, where $X_f$ is the locus where the germ of $f$ is a unit. Then the ideal generated by $s$ is the whole ring $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. No affineness of the opens is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering; last two paragraphs of proof, lines 365-388

proof.text: Enumerate $s$ as $f_1,\ldots,f_n$. The map $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_X$ with coordinates $f_i$ is surjective: at each point at least one $f_i$ is a stalk unit. Its kernel $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent. Set $\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F\cap\mathcal O_X^{\oplus i}$ using the first $i$ summands. Projection to coordinate $i$ identifies $\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1}$ with a quasi-coherent ideal subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$.

Start with $H^1(X,\mathcal F_0)=0$ since $\mathcal F_0=0$. In the long exact sequence for $0\to\mathcal F_{i-1}\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1}\to0$, the segment in degree one has zero outer terms by induction and the ideal vanishing hypothesis. Therefore $H^1(X,\mathcal F_i)=0$, and finally $H^1(X,\mathcal F)=0$.

The initial segment for $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_X\to0$ now makes the map on global sections surjective. A preimage of $1$ gives $a_i$ with $\sum_i a_i f_i=1$. Thus $1$ belongs to the generated ideal. If $s$ is empty, the cover forces $X$ empty and its section ring is the zero ring, so the conclusion still holds.
